t: Synthetic transactions — Archive Service Health Checker
title: Synthetic transactions — Archive Service Health Checker
description:
The archive service health checker watches every service the archive depends on — search clusters, storage, metadata APIs, external sources — and reports availability, latency, and correctness continuously. It probes from the caller's perspective with synthetic transactions, so 'up' means 'actually serving correct results', not just 'port open'. Health data feeds routing, alerting, and the reliability dashboard.

This record documents the synthetic transactions approach: Run realistic end-to-end probes (search, fetch, write) on a schedule against every service.

Teaching ladder rank 1 (foundations): this record explains the core idea in plain terms — what inputs the tool takes, what outputs it produces, and when it is the right choice for an archive task.

Every record in this database is the full fully-formed file with all data — never a stub or description alone. This database holds 15 of the 1,000,000 target — the march to a million is in progress.
demo:
# Archive Service Health Checker demo: synthetic probes -> availability + SLO.
import random
random.seed(7)
SERVICES=["search","storage","metadata"]
def probe(svc):
    ok=random.random()>0.1
    lat=random.randint(20,120) if ok else None
    correct=ok and random.random()>0.05
    return ok,lat,correct
for s in SERVICES:
    results=[probe(s) for _ in range(20)]
    avail=sum(1 for o,_,c in results if o and c)/len(results)
    lats=sorted(l for _,l,_ in results if l)
    p99=lats[int(0.99*(len(lats)-1))] if lats else None
    print("%s availability=%.2f p99=%sms SLO=%s"%(s,avail,p99,"MET" if avail>=0.99 else "BREACHED"))
provenance: Public-harvest: documents established, real-world methods for archive service health checker; fact-checked public knowledge.
